title: Now available: Cross-region Link to Fabric and Update connection

body_markdown:
Link to Fabric helps customers bring Microsoft Dataverse data into Fabric without building and maintaining complex data pipelines. Today, we are announcing two updates that make creating and managing these links simpler and more resilient:


• **Cross-region Link to Fabric:** Connect any Dataverse region to any Microsoft Fabric region.


• **Update connection:** Change the connection used by an existing Fabric link without unlinking and recreating it.


Both improvements address common sources of customer friction and give organizations more flexibility in how they configure and operate Link to Fabric.


# Connect any Dataverse region to any Fabric region


Until now, customers had to consider the region and Azure geography of both their Dataverse environment and Fabric workspace before creating a link.


Terms such as “same Azure geography” and “same region” were not always clear. Customers also did not always know where their Dataverse environment was hosted. This led to trial and error, failed setup attempts, and delays before they could begin working with their data.


We have now removed this regional alignment requirement.


Customers can create a Link to Fabric from **any Dataverse region to any Microsoft Fabric region** . You can choose the Fabric workspace that best fits your organization’s data strategy, existing analytics footprint, and operational needs, regardless of where the Dataverse environment is hosted.


This means:


• No region-matching guesswork


• More flexibility when choosing a Fabric workspace


• A simpler path from business data to analytics and AI


Cross-region fabric link is generally available now.


# Update the connection used by an existing Fabric link


We are also introducing the ability to update the connection used by an existing Link to Fabric.


Connections may need to change throughout the lifecycle of a link. A link might have been created with an incorrect configuration, an individual user might change roles or leave the organization, a service account password might change, or organizational policies might require a different service account or authentication method. Customers may also want to move from a user or service account to Fabric workspace identity.


Previously, changing the connection required customers to unlink Fabric and create the link again. That was disruptive and added avoidable operational overhead.


With **Update connection** , you can seamlessly change to a different existing connection or create a new connection without changing your existing sync.


From the Fabric link details page, select **Update connection** from the command bar.


In the update experience, choose another connection or create a new one. Where available, we recommend using **workspace identity** so the link is not dependent on an individual user account.


# Why workspace identity matters


Individual user and service accounts require organizations to manage account ownership, credentials, and lifecycle changes. Workspace identity is tied to the Fabric workspace instead.


Using workspace identity helps reduce the risk of a link being affected when an employee changes roles or leaves the organization. It provides a more durable authentication model for business-critical CRM and ERP analytics workloads.


Customers who created a link with a user or service account can use **Update connection** to select or create a connection that uses workspace identity, without changing their existing sync.


Connection update is currently rolling out across regions and would be available across regions by end of November 2026


# A simpler and more resilient experience


These updates remove two significant sources of friction:


1. **Where you connect:** Any Dataverse region can now connect to any Fabric region.


2. **How you connect:** The connection behind an existing link can now be changed without recreating the link.


Together, they make Link to Fabric easier to adopt, simpler to manage, and more resilient as organizations and their analytics environments evolve.


This is another meaningful step toward making Link to Fabric a first-class analytics experience for CRM and ERP. We listened to your feedback, and we will continue simplifying the path from business data to insights and AI.
